newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian shares end off lows, Rao hearing delayed.
newsitem.headline: Indian shares end off lows, Rao hearing delayed.

text.p: Indian shares ended mixed but off their lows as punters covered short positions after the criminal court postponed a hearing involving former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao until next week, traders said.
Share prices in Bombay ended lower but the Delhi and Calcutta stocks indices closed slightly higher.
"The market was expecting some news on Rao's arrest and when it got delayed by a week, speculators ran to cover short positions," said a Bombay-based trader.
Rao's plea for protection against possible arrest was turned down last week.
On Monday, the supreme court said it exempted Rao from appearing in court on the same day due to security threats.

Traders said most funds remained on the sidelines but some were sellers in blue chips including TELCO and MTNL. Shares of State Bank of India were hammered to 248.25 in early trade on the BSE before rebounding to end 1.25 rupees up at 252.75.
Traders said funds were selling the underlying ahead of the firm's GDR pricing. They said was unlikely SBI would achieve its indicative pricing of 275 rupees in weak market conditions.
Petrochemicals firm Reliance told the BSE its board would meet on October 18 to approve 1996/97 first half results.

Shares of cable maker Sterlite fell 28.75 rupees to 185.75 on the BSE ahead of results for the year ended June 30, 1996. The firm said its net climbed to 1.4 billion rupees after a merger with group firm Sterlite Communications.
The merger -- effective from April 1 -- was passed by shareholders but is awaiting court approval.
The Delhi index closed 5.03 points higher at 722.24 on bids by foreign funds and speculators. The Calcutta index gained 3.54 points to 424.61.

Voting began in northern Uttar Pradesh state for crucial local assembly polls where Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's United Front alliance takes on the Congress party and the BJP in a triangular fight.
